comment: Dystopo data source registry (docs/PLANNING.md > Licensing, hard rule 4). Every data source used to build anything we ship is listed here with its license and required attribution. Outputs compose their attribution from this file through SourceRegistry; don't hard-code credits elsewhere. kind: dem | geoid | osm (inputs to the OSM vector tile build) | overlay | font (fonts the app draws labels with). license is an SPDX id or expression (ids joined with AND / OR / WITH), or LicenseRef-* where SPDX has none.

sources.name: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 Public
sources.provider: European Union / ESA (Copernicus Programme); WorldDEM by DLR and Airbus; hosted on AWS Open Data by Sinergise

coverage.summary: Global land, except a small set of GLO-30 tiles not released to the public; no tiles over open ocean.

sources.licenseName: Copernicus DEM licence (free for the general public)
sources.attribution: Elevation: Copernicus DEM GLO-30, produced using Copernicus WorldDEM-30 © DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA; all rights reserved.

sources.allowedUses: Free use, modification and redistribution of derived products (including commercial) with the required credit.
sources.updateCadence: Static (2021 release); the public tile list can change.
sources.notes: Surface model (DSM): includes forest canopy and buildings, so it sits above bare-earth DEMs in forest. 1x1 degree Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs named by their south-west corner.

sources.name: USGS 3DEP 1/3 arc-second DEM
sources.provider: U.S. Geological Survey, 3D Elevation Program (The National Map)

coverage.summary: Conterminous US, Hawaii, US territories and parts of Alaska; seamless.

sources.attribution: Elevation: USGS 3D Elevation Program (3DEP) 1/3 arc-second DEM, courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey (public domain).
sources.attributionHtml: Elevation: USGS 3DEP 1/3 arc-second DEM, courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey (public domain).
sources.allowedUses: Unrestricted. USGS asks that it be credited as the source.
sources.updateCadence: Rolling: cells are refreshed in 'current' as new lidar is incorporated, several times a year.
sources.notes: 1x1 degree Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs named by their north-west corner, NAD83 geographic. Converted to EGM2008 with the hybrid geoid covering each cell (geoid18 in CONUS, geoid18-prvi in Puerto Rico / USVI, geoid12b-alaska, geoid12b-hawaii) and egm2008; not fetched where no hybrid geoid covers.

sources.name: USGS 3DEP 1 m lidar DEM
sources.provider: U.S. Geological Survey, 3D Elevation Program (The National Map)

coverage.summary: Patchy, project by project, across the US; growing. Found through the TNM Access API.

sources.attribution: Elevation: USGS 3D Elevation Program (3DEP) 1 m lidar DEM, courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey (public domain).
sources.attributionHtml: Elevation: USGS 3DEP 1 m lidar DEM, courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey (public domain).
sources.allowedUses: Unrestricted. USGS asks that it be credited as the source.
sources.updateCadence: Continuous: new lidar projects are published as surveys are processed.
sources.notes: 10x10 km tiles in NAD83 / UTM, grouped by survey project; newer surveys are composited on top. Bare earth. Converted to EGM2008 with the hybrid geoid covering each cell (geoid18, geoid18-prvi, geoid12b-alaska, geoid12b-hawaii) and egm2008.

sources.name: swisstopo swissALTI3D
sources.provider: Federal Office of Topography swisstopo

coverage.summary: Switzerland and Liechtenstein, in 1x1 km LV95 tiles. Tiles straddling the border are filled across the whole tile (seen at the Matterhorn), so coverage ends in a 1 km staircase up to a kilometre beyond the border.

sources.resolution: 2 m (used to z15) and 0.5 m (used where output cells are under 2 m)
sources.licenseName: Terms of use for free geodata and geoservices (OGD) from swisstopo, 26 August 2022: free use for all purposes, including commercial, with the source indicated
sources.attribution: Elevation: swissALTI3D © swisstopo (Federal Office of Topography swisstopo).
sources.attributionHtml: Elevation: swissALTI3D © swisstopo (Federal Office of Topography swisstopo).
sources.allowedUses: Free use, processing and redistribution, including commercial, with the source indicated next to the data or in accompanying documentation (derived products may say derived from).
sources.updateCadence: Six-year update cycle; tiles are re-flown region by region and published under a new year in their item id.
sources.notes: Bare-earth DTM. Found through the swisstopo STAC API (cached per 0.1 degree cell); each item is one 1x1 km tile with Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF assets (2 m: 500x500 px, 128 px LZW tiles, one 4 m overview; 0.5 m: 2000x2000 px with 1, 2 and 4 m overviews), no-data -9999. Reprojected from LV95 with the rigorous swisstopo formulas (mm-level against the published REFRAME points). Heights converted LN02 -> EGM2008 with chgeo2004 (ETRS89 taken as WGS84, a few cm) and egm2008; the conversion error is that of the two geoid models, a few cm for CHGeo2004 plus EGM2008's own decimetre-level error in the Alps. Composited over Copernicus with a 300 m feather; only read where output cells are 30 m or finer (z12 and up).

sources.name: Kartverket national detailed height model (DTM)
sources.provider: Kartverket (Norwegian Mapping Authority)

coverage.summary: Mainland Norway, plus a strip of smoother, coarser data reaching 10 km or more into Sweden along the land border (seen at Storlien); sea and everything beyond the strip are 0 in the service and treated as no data, so Copernicus fills there.

sources.resolution: 1 m (national lidar and image matching; read through the WCS at 1 to 16 m)
sources.attribution: Elevation: national detailed height model (DTM) © Kartverket (CC BY 4.0).
sources.attributionHtml: Elevation: national detailed height model (DTM) © Kartverket (CC BY 4.0).
sources.allowedUses: Free use, adaptation and redistribution, including commercial, with attribution to Kartverket.
sources.updateCadence: Continuous: new lidar blocks replace older data as they are processed.
sources.notes: Bare-earth DTM (nhm_dtm_topo_25833). There are no range-readable COGs: the open download (hoydedata.no) is zipped project blocks, so the source asks the WCS (an ArcGIS image service) for fixed 256x256 px blocks on a UTM 33 grid at 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 m (nearest neighbour), about 260 kB each, and caches every block on disk; at most 4 requests in flight. Heights converted NN2000 -> EGM2008 with href2018b (ETRS89 taken as WGS84) and egm2008. Composited over Copernicus with a 300 m feather; only read where output cells are 30 m or finer (z12 and up in Norway).

sources.name: BEV ALS DTM Austria (Hoehenraster 1 m)
sources.provider: Bundesamt fuer Eich- und Vermessungswesen (BEV), with the Austrian federal states (geoland.at)

coverage.summary: Austria, in 55 tiles of 50x50 km on the EPSG:3035 grid; cells outside Austria are no data, so coverage follows the border exactly (seen at the Weisskugel on the Italian border).

sources.resolution: 1 m (airborne laser scanning), with internal overviews to 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 m and coarser
sources.verticalDatum: EVRF2000 Austria (EPSG:9274, orthometric) on ETRS89 / LAEA Europe (EPSG:3035); the 2021 edition alone was in GHA (EPSG:5778)
sources.attribution: Elevation: ALS DTM © BEV, Austrian federal and state geodata providers (CC BY 4.0).
sources.attributionHtml: Elevation: ALS DTM © BEV, Austrian federal and state geodata providers (CC BY 4.0).
sources.allowedUses: Free use, adaptation and redistribution, including commercial, with attribution to BEV.
sources.updateCadence: Yearly editions (Stichtag 15 September), each a full set of 55 tiles; the source pins one edition.
sources.notes: Bare-earth DTM from the BEV INSPIRE download service (ATOM feed of series eae5f98d-d605-4783-8292-8b913d163cac). Each tile is a Cloud-Optimized BigTIFF of about 7.7 GB (50001x50001 float32, 512 px LZW tiles with the floating-point predictor, overviews), read with range requests only for the blocks a window needs. Reprojected from EPSG:3035 with LambertAzimuthalEqualArea (EPSG guidance-note formulas). Heights converted EVRF2000 Austria -> EGM2008 with bev-geoid (ETRS89 taken as WGS84) and egm2008. Composited over Copernicus with a 300 m feather; only read where output cells are 30 m or finer (z12 and up).

sources.name: OpenFreeMap planet vector tiles
sources.provider: OpenFreeMap (openfreemap.org), public instance at tiles.openfreemap.org; built from OpenStreetMap with the OpenMapTiles schema

coverage.summary: Global, z0-14 Web Mercator vector tiles.

sources.licenseName: ODbL 1.0 (the OpenStreetMap data); OpenMapTiles schema CC-BY 4.0
sources.attribution: Tiles: OpenFreeMap
sources.attributionHtml: OpenFreeMap
sources.allowedUses: Free public instance: no keys, no registration, no request limits, commercial use allowed (openfreemap.org FAQ). Required credit: OpenFreeMap (optional but asked), (c) OpenMapTiles, Data from OpenStreetMap; always compose this entry with openmaptiles and osm.
sources.updateCadence: Weekly planet builds; the TileJSON at the url names the current versioned tile path (immutable, cacheable).
sources.notes: Used only by devtool serve --live, outside region packs: each missing z/x/y is fetched once and cached on disk under <cache>/openfreemap/<build>/. The schema is OpenMapTiles 3.16, so the default style's outdoors-only layers (outdoor_poi, natural_line, wilderness) match nothing there.

sources.name: Overpass API (raw OpenStreetMap for a box)
sources.provider: Overpass API public instance overpass-api.de (FOSSGIS); serves current OpenStreetMap data

coverage.summary: Global; Dystopo asks it only for small boxes (default at most 0.05 square degrees).

sources.resolution: Vector (raw OSM nodes, ways and relations)
sources.attribution: © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL 1.0)
sources.attributionHtml: © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL 1.0)
sources.allowedUses: Usage policy of the public instances (dev.overpass-api.de/overpass-doc/en/preface/commons.html, wiki Overpass_API): fewer than about 10000 requests and 1 GB per day per user, no parallel scripts, no scraping by stitching boxes, a timeout and maxsize on heavy queries, back off after 429 (rate limit) and 504 (server load). Dystopo sends one request per pack build with a descriptive User-Agent, a timeout and a maxsize, caches the answer per box and never retries automatically.
sources.updateCadence: Minutely replication of OpenStreetMap.
sources.notes: Used by devtool serve --live for POST /build?profile=outdoors (OverpassSource.kt): one [out:xml] query per box, cached under <cache>/overpass/, converted to .osm.pbf and built with tilebuild's outdoors profile. Same credit as osm, so composed attribution shows it once.

sources.attributionHtml: Labels: Noto Sans, © The Noto Project Authors (SIL OFL 1.1).
